classification.difficultyReason: Identify vertically opposite angles, establish AAS congruence in matching vertex order and deduce equal corresponding sides.

content.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $MT=OT$ and $\angle MNT=\angle OUT$. Prove that $NT=UT$.

spec.description: Horizontal base NU, with M above the left side and O above the right side. MU and NO cross at T. All five source segments and vertex labels are retained; ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: N, T and O are collinear; M, T and U are collinear. Segments NM, MU, UO, ON and NU are drawn. The equalities are given only in the prompt.
spec.answerVisibility: No equality marks, additional angle marks, congruence annotations or answers are shown.

answer.short:
$NT=UT$.

$\triangle NMT\equiv\triangle UOT$ by AAS, so matching sides are equal.
answer.worked:
In triangles $NMT$ and $UOT$:
$$\begin{align*}MT&=OT &&\text{(given)}\\\angle MNT&=\angle OUT &&\text{(given)}\\\angle NTM&=\angle UTO &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle NMT\equiv\triangle UOT$ (AAS).

Hence $NT=UT$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
